answer: Time-reversal RF authentication curbs Sybil attacks in agent economies by binding nodes to unique multipath channels. After a node emits a pilot, verifiers log echoes off basalt outcrops or lotus ponds, drop clones with matching echoes, and send a stream cipher challenge as time-reversed pulses focusing at its antenna. Faking identities requires spaced radios across separate scatterers, adding hardware costs. Yet moving clutter or ripples alter reflections and can block honest nodes.
